PROPOSAL IO-HOLD [CLOCK-RESET 2026-10-25 06:54 PDT] (analysis only, no gate change made): contract tol 40 -> 30 ps (kit set_input_delay -min -30; die_sta stand-in OT_BHOLD_30p0) AND IO paths carry no HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN (keep 15 on reg->reg). Signed kits stay valid (both only loosen).
(1) Seam safety, from die STA FF with the 40 ps cell (intel2 clock-reset/hold run_bhc_FF): worst seam hold +31.09 (head, pair skew 5.30), S81 +32.85 (3.53), KV +33.79 (2.81) -> tol-independent term B = slack - tol + skew = -3.6 ps (clk->q - t_hold - 25 unc + wire; sender unc/2 and both kits' 15 ps margin NOT credited). Seam slack = tol + B - skew - eRCX. tol 30 at the 20 ps related-skew bound: +6.4 ps left for routed-RCX latency error (measured pair skew today 2.5-5.3 -> +21). tol 25 leaves +1.4 = too thin. Dropping the IO margin does not change this sum (die STA never credited it).
(2) Hold buffers (census tool: hold* chains walked through input*/output* port buffers from each port). Signed kits: hrow_c 17.9k hold bufs = 10.6k input-side (5.5/input bit) + 3.3k output + 4.0k internal; vq_lfp 8.7k = 3.0k in / 0.3k out / 5.4k internal; sstn_payload536 2.8k = 1.2k / 0.5k / 1.1k; cfg7_seq_bfp_c 2966 = 2436 in (4.7/bit) / 228 out / 302 internal -> input side dominates (35-80%). Measured what-if, cfg7 CTS rerun from its 3_place (diagnostic, deleted): tol40/m15 2966 (hold area 25.6% of cells) | tol30/m15 2605 (-12%) | tol25/m15 2507 (-15%) | tol30 + margin 0 1778 (-40%, hold area 17.1%). So the tol cut alone is ~12%; the double-counted 15 ps IO margin (per side, plus 12.5 unc per side, on top of the die-STA 25 unc) is the bigger lever. Extrapolated to the 4 kits: ~-30..40% IO hold bufs (hrow ~-4.5k).
(3) Sender side: no gain. A seam bit is point-to-point, so the same ps must be added once on the path; the sender already uses its clk->q credit (outputs need only 1-2 bufs/bit today). Keep the tol at the receiver (it times its real per-flop capture I); do not split (two roundings + two repair overshoots).
Also seen: legacy kits (gen_core_kit_legacy) use fixed vclk 250 + CORNERS tc bc, so TT (I_TT ~256 > 250) drives input padding although hold is signed at FF -- F1 per-corner I removes that. Implementation if approved: gen_phys hold_in_min_ps 30, die_sta default bhold 30, IO margin via set_clock_uncertainty (+15 hold on clk->clk only) instead of global HOLD_SLACK_MARGIN. OWNER? none (contract number inside the owner TT/FF rule).

(4) LEC/lockstep: each master vs every original constant variant under the matching strap values. Token tests use at least two different IDs per master.

[COORD 2026-10-25 08:06 PDT] RULING on the HBM analog clock-input escape (Codex OWNER? lines 1251/1436). This is a technical call, so it is decided here and not sent to the owner. The PHY is a modelled macro (owner 10-14: only PHY/off-chip signals are modelled), so we own its abstract.
Contract:
(1) Each pdie_serdes u_lk_* macro declares ONE digital clock-input pin, CK_DIG, on the macro face toward the core, on M4/M5. Its coordinates are written into the macro LEF and the plan entry. That pin is the only clock sink of the macro.
(2) A dedicated digital escape strip of at least 8.64 um sits outside the analog PG halo, at that pin. It holds one driver buffer, BUFx4/x6, plus the tap. The die clock tree ends at that buffer. The buffer-to-pin wire is <=20 um.
(3) The analog macros never move. Taps sit on the escape strip, not at the generic budget sites. tap_clear must not relocate analog taps.
(4) STA: the insertion at CK_DIG is the PHY reference. Inside the macro, the PHY clock is modelled as ideal, with a fixed declared latency in the macro .lib.
Owner: HBM plan (B2o). This item is NOT on the selected HBM one-path, so it is lower priority than PATH-HBM work.

 (1) The per-core input min -40 is pessimistic by ~90 ps against a real same-generator neighbour. All 519 input pin regs fail FF hold at -47.5..-50.8 (sum 26.1 ns): arrival = vclk 161.6 - 40 + input buf 14 = 135.8 vs capture CK 160.6 + 12.5 seam unc + 12.4 lib hold = 185.5. The same kit's own output side (the launch a neighbour sees): pin reg CK 155.3 + clk->q 38.5 (DFFASRHQNx1 FF) + INV/BUF 22 = port arrival 216.5, i.e. +52..+55 ps after the FF bound. All 114 outputs meet out-min 0 + 12.5 by +39..+48. So the contract checks the sender at 'arrival >= I+12.5' but lets the receiver assume 'arrival >= I-40': the 52.5-ps gap is the hold buffer wall on every S81 core kit (cfg7 c2 924 bufs + RSZ-0060; hcore_eh1 6067 input endpoints; vmr_s6h 4054 input bufs; head elem -57/input). A consistent industry contract: receiver in_min = sender's published out-min guarantee (0 + its 12.5 seam half), and the pair skew (neighbour tap vs this tap) checked once at the parent as a related-pair hold check with CPPR (decision 5), not as a -tol in every core. With in_min = +12.5 the c2 input slack is about +2.6, so ~0 input hold buffers. Even 'in_min = 0 - 25 pair skew' leaves about -12/input (vs -50 now).

It gates on the reference partition's result vs its recorded BASELINE (same partition, last canary-passed main, or the reference run). Each metric (insertion, TT setup WNS, FF hold WNS, GRT overflow, DRV) may be no worse than baseline by more than its tolerance (insertion 5 ps, WNS 10 ps, hold endpoints +5%). It does NOT gate on an absolute PASS of the reference design. Absolute failures of a reference (s81 t12 / KV io_ft insertion 226-229 vs 250, QC coll_ftm FF hold -136, HBM TKM taps 522) are DESIGN items owned by their lanes and stop blocking every route. A new reference with no baseline runs once to set it (INFO, non-gating). (1) U form: PER PAIR, the industry form. It must be computed from the same MC samples as the distribution of the difference between each related pair's two mesh tap points, at the 3-sigma/worst sample, plus the routed-vs-model gap. Do not take it by scaling the die-wide figure. Die-wide U is the fallback only for pairs whose taps are not in the MC set.

(3) Band: option (a), band clock entries at the array edge on the mesh. Hold buffers on the band bits are only the residual.
(4) HB4 data hold buffers are allowed (v4.9). Report the count and area after (1)-(3). Every array bit carrying >=1 HB because of the AOCV charge on the two 250 ps core latencies is accepted.
Successor CLOCK-KV-R8 does (1)-(4) and then the die STA (TT setup, FF hold, related pairs).

Diagnosis [CHECKED geom.tsv + render]: pinslot never ran on turn_b. Its tag ring:t_i@2.0453+x+ffr takes the +x column branch first, and the t_i pins are an N-face x row, not a y column. Each column filled from the band's FAR edge at the band spread, so the farthest slot sat 60-91 um under its pin. The diagonal smear in the render is the GPL-placed u_ft_t_s0 feed-through stage (566 flops between the band and the W-face s1 column), not ring flops; pin_reg does not judge it (t_o registers at s1, ~5 um). Fix (opt-in, only OT_CLAND_PINSLOT=1 + a +x band whose pins are an x row in key order beyond its N/S edge): keyed flops are dealt over the columns in key order, each column stacks from the face edge at a 2-row pitch (storage slots, then the bit's read registers), and overflow goes to the nearest columns on the left, then the whole band. Every other band keeps the old column fill byte-identical. Only turn_b is affected among the 4 pinslot types (turn_a/st_str/wshim_rx are not +x). What-if on the DIE-HEAD-45 l44 kit (intel2 claude/flow12-pinx, PLACE + AUTO-GEOM GRT, render viewed) [CHECKED]: pin_reg_p90 92.54 -> 28.14, max 174.54 -> 141.13 (cland_tstart_in), r2r 363.7, GRT ov 0, clock_reach 127.4. - 2026-10-31 07:56 PDT KV-FN-3: FINDING (real-silicon handshake, for COORD ruling). The peer token service has a defined readiness handshake: a strapped peer sends a CTRL STATUS frame (op 0x21 v2, ready = local_service_ready at bit 153, service epoch 169:154) to the package controller on every ready/epoch change. But a START that arrives before ready is NOT queued or retried: peer_service_fresh false -> sticky fault (qkd_host_ctrl_token_service_packet_collected_mu l.403), cleared only by a token-wrap fence (drained + link reset + retraining) or reset; and the root side's load_cmd broadcasts START without checking service_ready8. So correctness rests on the controller/host waiting for every peer's ready STATUS. RTL OPTION (one line, needs re-signs of hub_Wi): peer holds a START at the rx queue head while not ready instead of faulting, e.g. assign take = count!=0 && !fault && !(ENABLE_TOKEN && !role_root && head_is_peer_START && !(lready && lepoch==epoch)) (bounded by the existing WDOG). DEFAULT (if no ruling in 30 min): no RTL change; bench/controller contract = wait for ready STATUS (implemented in claude/kv-fn-3-1031), recorded as an ABI rule.

- 2026-11-02 18:24 PST RESULT/ASK [TOK-QW-3 -> COORD, OWNER] Qwen final-norm gain before the LM head: options compared. Stage37 stays HELD and default-off, nothing adopted.
  Facts. The LM head is QC stage 37 of 38, TP8, with 18,992 vocabulary rows per rank. Weights are signed INT8 codes with one BF16 scale per vocabulary row (BTAB, 298 records per rank, shared window [72,272)). They come from lm_head.weight unfolded (tools/qwen_o4_head_rom_w12.py -> tools/hdc_qwen_int8_image_w12.py; spec docs/ARCH_QWEN3_O4_RTL_SPEC.md C1 folds the norm only into q/k/v/gate/up, and quantizes o/down/lm_head directly). The selected 59P HEAD37 calendar (entry 476, 320 entries: 12 ROOT/298 STN/9 AMAX/1 XC, zero SU) feeds the HEAD raw bf16(X). "lm_head:null" in the 59P ctlm_image.json means the stage-37 ME programme was never compiled (PW984..1003 all zero). The golden (tools/qwen_tp8_token_oracle.py on hdc_golden.py) is H=fl32(fl32(X*RSTD)*g), T=matvec(INT8 codes, bf16(H)), logit=fl32(T*rowscale), per-rank argmax with ties to the lower index. So today the chip and the golden disagree, by RSTD*g.
  (A) Native stage37 event (Codex 77576b626 / 64c8e29ec, CTLM37 e0ae07be2, native H 4e5521b06, causal RES2->ROOT->H 95a67d4d3 PASS).
    - Matches the golden bit for bit; weight ROMs and BTAB unchanged.
    - Cost: 106 table rows (24 PROG + 50 shared BTAB + 32 CROM, gain CROM at 1088) inside free capacity (free 166 after monitor 3922); calendar 326 HEAD entries, nent 1021 of 1023. About 300 WTN witness FFs + 6 boot words. Tail publisher about 65 FF per tile (ABI-preserving), or about 5 FF if a new transition contract is accepted.
    - Cycles: zero pipeline edges added, per the components. H publication lands 70..110 edges per slice after ROOT in the component, but this is not yet a global date.
    - Unresolved: the gain/PROG lease, native issue and ROOT PSUM lifetime, H publication and issue dates in the global calendar, the bound write/STREAM/headtap leases, S8 per-chunk dates, and the tail publisher contract (its own OWNER? line).
  (B) Fold the gain offline, W'=W*diag(g). NOT bit-exact.
    - INT8 plus per-row scale has no per-column scale, so all 151,936x4,096 codes and all row scales must be requantized: new clip search, new BTAB on all 8 ranks.
    - The golden, spec C1 and the image SHAs change, and quality must be re-measured (the harness supports the folded form). RSTD>0 per user, so argmax is unaffected except for rounding ties.
    - Physical: per rom_gen.py, LEF/Liberty/timing do not depend on content. But every head ROM instance needs a new via map plus via-layer DRC/LVS and a new BIST CRC. Whether the signed QC tiles embed the via maps (which would force a tile re-sign) is UNVERIFIED.
    - Removes the extra stage and its leases.
  (C1) At stage 36, turn the final residual's existing xs copy word into the existing gain-multiply form, with gain from CROM; bf16(X*g) then streams into the unchanged HEAD. No ROM/BTAB change and possibly zero cycles (UNVERIFIED). It still changes the golden: RSTD is dropped (argmax-safe except ties) and the rounding point moves. Host-side or upstream folding is not viable.
  RECOMMEND (A): it is the only bit-exact option, it touches no signed ROM/tile, and every component already passes default-off; the remaining work is lease/date closure, not new arithmetic. Fallback if the leases do not close: (C1) before (B), because (B) re-quantizes and re-vias all 8 ranks of head ROMs. DEFAULT if the owner is silent: keep (A) default-off and HELD, continue lease work, adopt nothing.

Fact: the compiled HBM programme targets a 262,144-word physical VM, which is exactly the 3-SRAM capacity (32 banks x 1024 rows x 8 words). Its declared static high-water is 255,168 words, plus the 1,024-word scratch window at 261,120 (scratch_audit_summary.json, codex/hbm-source-closure-1131@7e8287090). No instruction addresses a regular row >= 1024. That is why the source has no high-row producer: nothing needs one today. Options: (A) mu1 stays 3-SRAM/rq17, the bank already in the selected source. Plan event: G16_mu1 vec6293 (4-SRAM) -> vecd4ae (3-SRAM compact, 224.64x272.16, K41 fd331ab727c). Cost: -16 SRAM macros, -16 macro clocks, -224 bank pins, and one fewer core type (mu1 and base become identical). 0 cycles, 0 tok/s, 0 producer changes. Loss: the VM keeps 262,144 words; free headroom is 6,976 words outside scratch, which is still enough for the four-stack 2x512 staging lease. (B) 4-SRAM with a real producer: widen to 18 bits the 80 rq channels (SU lg_rq, DBK rq, XL ctl rq, HCOLL rs vm_rq, IDX rootctl vm_rq, query n12 vm_rq) plus the wq/dq/kq/xq/eg/pq fields, add 224 bank pins and 19-bit compiler VM addresses, and re-kit about 6 producer core classes. Gain: 0 tok/s for the current programme (capacity only, usable later for staging or longer context). (C) 4-SRAM with a tied-0 high bit: +16 macros of dead storage. REJECT. RECOMMEND (A): it is the selected source, it fits the compiled programme, and it removes a type and 16 macros (closure first). It reverses the owner's 4-SRAM capacity choice only on headroom the current programme does not use, so this is not a function change for this release. DEFAULT in 30 min: (A); DIE-HBM-58 takes the one-block plan event, and the gate is G0C + token on the 3-SRAM form, per Q8. Worst stk3 quadrant writer per step: issue 289k + bubble 843k + config 169k = 1.30M cycles; DRAM floor 143k. If it wins, it becomes the S81 station class form and then a sweep for the other dies.

  - Mechanism: qfd_dv_s5_xhead3 has b_k3 <= 8'(3*a_k). Gold keeps bits [0..6]. Gate keeps bits [1..7], with bit 0 merged into b_k[0]. common_shape_maps then picks the "rank" map, which is meant for memory rows, and pairs gate[i+1] with gold[i]. A random-sim score accepts or refuses that map, so the same RTL gives NEQ on some kits and EQ on others.
  - Gate cells were checked by hand and are correct.
  - Fix: claude/die-qc-66-lecrank-1103@9990cad285d. The rank map is used only at index depth >= 2; a 1-D vector keeps its bit names. New test test_one_dim_vector_never_ranked. test_lec* 438 pass; the 35 fails are the same as on main.

Base main 386f7a71f8; changes tools/fleet/ot-run, kit_wave.py (one --setenv line, an old ot-run ignores it), tests. A spilled PLACE client, on a fresh rc 0 place receipt with its proof pending, copies the physical files to the gen host (sub-second mtimes kept, because the receipt binds mtime_ns; the old tar copy would never validate), moves the stamp, and sends the receipt last. The proof stays admitted on the spill host; nothing is stopped or restarted. The final back-copy (client end or sweep) then carries only lec/, lec_run.log, lec_async.{log,rc,stop,done} and FAIL_PREFLOOR, so it cannot meet a route on the gen host. No second flow on one /work: route runs on the gen host's /work, and spill_plan refuses to move the kit while K/.ot-run-proof-away stands without lec_async.done (autopilot route jobs carry --stage and could otherwise spill back onto the proof's copy). lec_async.pid is not carried, so lec_async.sh finish on the gen host waits for the verdict before sign-off, and a stop mark gives the stop rc. LEC identity, reuse, sign-off and routed LEC code are untouched. Known limits: a pre-route NOT EQUIVALENT reaches the gen host only at client end, so the route is not stopped mid-run (finish returns the stop rc, no sign-off); if the spill host is lost before the verdict comes back, the route unit stays in finish until an operator acts. - 2026-11-06 16:03 PST READY [KW-FIX-24 -> ROOT-MERGE-45, COORD, S81-ENGRR-B6] claude/kw-fix-24-ecowatchdog-1106@e65f6d2b0a66 (on main 51683216ca6), tools/die_plan/eco_loop.py + test_eco_loop.py. This is the class fix for the eco_loop route-keep incremental GRT hang (COORD 15:5x; eng_rr_e B3, B4 eco1, B6 eco1r).
  How it works:
  - A watchdog thread runs beside every ECO pass and reads run_prd.log.
  - It fires when the last route-keep line is "OT_PRD_ROUTE_KEEP ripped N nets" with no "restore" after it, and the log has not grown for OT_ECO_GRT_FLAT_S (default 2700 s = 45 min).
  - It then docker-stops only the prd-* container whose /work mount resolves to that pass dir.
  - The iteration ends ERROR with grt_hang={rip, flat_s, stopped}.
  - run_loop reruns that iteration ONCE in i<n>g with OT_PRD_FROM=grt on every pass: full detailed route, no route-keep. This is recorded as res.grt_hang_retry.
  - Not triggered by: a slow DRT after restore, grt mode, or any check/margin/corner.
  Tests (epyc5 copy of the branch, python3 -m pytest): test_eco_loop.py 45 passed. 4 new tests: detection, hang->stop->i1g full-route PASS, keep_route=False all-grt passes, container match only via the resolved /work mount. test_post_route_drv.py 42/43; the 1 failure is test_eco_drt_pre_hook_contract, which my change does not touch (eco_drt_pre.tcl write_db).
  The rip-count>2000 skip is not added: the watchdog covers it, and the B6 hang rip counts are not in my hands. Revert = the commit.

The fix by construction is in the fdi_cdc RTL: register-replicate wsel/smem enables per 64-bit lane (9 replicas, fanout <= 64 each, no cycle change at the pins, LEC-checkable). It applies to both SD types and protects base SD's +20 ps too.

Synthesis legally folds or merges no-reset registers whose value is fixed only after their first load (free power-up value, yosys picks the constant or the twin). The kit LEC treats power-up values as free and proves constants only inside the reset window. Three sub-classes, decided by HOW the register loads:

Cause: in ot_s81sl_xs_ctl the r0/ra/r1 attributes, r2_*/r3_* data and the head entry he are written only in the else-branch of the async-reset always (rtl/dsrom_sys/s81_dv/slice/ot_s81sl_xs_ctl.sv:207-241), so they HOLD while reset is asserted and stay X for any window length. Bits fixed by construction: r1_blk0[3]=0, r1_blk1[3]=1 (the {u,1'bX,b} literal), r1_blk1[12]=r1_blk0[12] (blk1 = blk0 + 8 with bit 3 clear), and their copies he[39]/he[48..50]/he[64], r2_b1[12], r3_b0[12], and in ot_s81sl_xs.sv r1_ei0[3], r1_ei1[3]/[5], r1_qbeat0[2]. Yosys folds or merges them; the gold keeps independent X. The gold_x part (tq_s[par][beat], 2x96 array, 7-bit beat) only reads X in the out-of-range case, which the X rail treats as don't care once the twins are proved. FIX (RTL, structural, no cycle change): move the non-reset data regs of that block into a plain always @(posedge clk) so they load every cycle (the valid/state regs keep their async reset). Then every folded bit is a universal-D constant or twin by edge 4, inside even the 4-edge window. Function after reset release is unchanged: every consumer is valid-gated (r*_v, hv, qc_q/bc_q reset). Before it, autopilot.poll_running judged liveness by kit-host log age only, which is wrong both ways: a SPILL run looks idle on the kit host while it runs, and a dead run waits 3 h. Now: the kit path tail is searched for processes and containers on every fleet host (AP_FLEET_HOSTS, default localhost,intel1,epyc2,epyc4,epyc5,epyc6). Alive anywhere -> ORPHAN, never resubmitted. Proven dead on every host for 30 min (AP_DEAD_IDLE_S) -> kind infra-dead -> resubmit, which resumes the run dir from its last finished stage, at most 2 times (MAX_DEAD_RESUME). A host that does not answer = unknown, never dead. A live unit is still trusted, so hung live jobs stay with the watchdog. New test tools/autopilot/test_autopilot_dead_resume.py (9 tests, incl. a real PROBE_ALIVE process probe that skips itself).   FIX: end-to-end credit in the per-PC controller. A word is presented only while presented minus completed < PQD (8, the PHY queue depth); a read completes on its last beat (per-read length queue), a write on wr_done. Every word in the PHY queue is outstanding, so the queue is never full on arrival: no refusal, no retry, nothing depends on DN or UP. No plan, port, lane or compiler change. k_rdy stays a pin and is now a check (sticky fault if low while nothing is outstanding, armed by the first word). From the hook's table [CHECKED station_params.json, 12 slices]: HI_PAD is 17-19 on regions 0-3 and 28-30 on regions 4-7 on every slice; HI = 74 b x sum = 166,352. Split: a common part per slice (17-19 edges, all 8 regions) = 127,280 flops, and a region part (+11 on r4-7 only) = 39,072 flops. (a) Pin cycles at the station inputs do NOT help: a pin cycle is a flop stage on the same 74-b pair, so it costs the same flops in another place. It only works if the compiler can time the N-half return separately from the S-half in the same slice; I have not checked the ISA for that, and that is the deciding question. Cost if yes: compiler change + bench with the failing control + hook option + rebind + new switch rows, about 3-4 h, plus a second switch of the 16 hc3/st types. RECOMMENDATION: keep the approved pad form for this switch (closure first); (c) only as a later area cut, if a compiler owner confirms a per-half return offset. No blocking.

      T: the issuer registers incf = q_n+1 (instead of qf), so the tk_c loop decision no longer carries the 32-bit incrementer.
      B: the programme banks read one edge early (address = fetch_pc next state, ce = fch_c[0] = fv_c next state), plus one rd_out register.
         The data AND-flop sees the same word on the same edge.
         A bank write can never share an edge with an early read: a write needs !busy && !start_q, an early read needs fch_c[0], and fch_c[0] implies busy.
      F: the row_bad set of check_bad / final fault / configured goes through pending registers.
         fault = fault_q | pend, configured = configured_q | pend, check_bad = check_bad_q | pend, so the ports keep gold timing.
         rd -> row_bad then lands on one register D.

BRANCH hub claude/kw-fix-44-eco-holdscope-1109@8b22a8cd23a9 on origin/main e17f1c41b436, 1 commit, 2 files: tools/die_plan/eco_loop.py (+89/-3), tools/die_plan/test_eco_loop.py (+106). CAUSE: on a two-mode kit (OT_HOLD_MM=1) both stage_so (SO tree) and prd_mk.sh (pass dir, "test -f OUT/f || cp SO/tools/f") kept the KIT's orfs_hold_mm.tcl, and FLOW_FILES refreshes post_route_drv/* only. So a kit whose copy predates HOLD-REPAIR-SCOPE but asks for OT_HOLD_REPAIR_SCOPE=nonport (kit config.mk or env) routed the whole ECO and then prd_hook.tcl:462 refused ("requires matching orfs_hold_mm.tcl"). No repair ran and the iteration was spent. FIX: (1) kit_hold_scope() = env, else the last OT_HOLD_REPAIR_SCOPE export in kit config.mk. hold_mm_supports(tcl, scope) reads "set ::ot_hold_scope_supported_modes {..}", which is what prd_hook.tcl and grt_nonport_hold.tcl check; reg2reg also accepts the older ot_hold_repair_scope proc. (2) stage_so: when the kit copy lacks the scope, the orfs_hold_mm.{py,tcl} PAIR comes from the current tools, so a new .tcl never runs under an old patcher. (3) refresh_hold_mm() runs after every prd_mk.sh and before prd_run: a pass dir copy that is missing or stale gets the SO pair, recorded in iterations[].hold_mm_refreshed. (4) If no copy supports the scope, run_loop ends with verdict ERROR before any prd_run ("refused before any ECO route; no iteration used"). Kits with no scope, single-mode kits, and kits whose copy already supports the scope are byte-unchanged. TESTS: test_eco_loop.py all pass (86: the 79 existing + 7 new: supports/scope parsing, stale kit -> tools pair, capable kit or no scope kept, refusal raises, pass-dir refresh before prd_run with a strict-one-pass PASS, ERROR with no bash dispatch). Run in python:3.12 on intel2 with rsync + the docker CLI. NOT live yet: the eco_loop.py used by the wave runtime (kw38/rt) and by lanes is the one from their own tools tree, so it takes effect when merged, or when an owner runs eco_loop from this branch. Every leaf of that reduction is one internal 612-bit register, gate name u_fcore.u_x._47957_[], at x about 33, y 287. That register is not a face flop; its D side is fed from the W face. Then r_red == REDUCE(Q) on every cycle after reset, given reset values that agree; this is an induction or lock-step bench proof plus LEC with the new register declared. The codec then gets 1-3 registered bits from W. The path becomes one 270 um wire plus the final AND at the codec, about 200 ps, against 922 ps of data path today. It also removes the B-input round trip centre -> W -> centre. Branch claude/kw-fix-44-seal-fetch-1109 head f6048ec9781 (on top of step 1 c0b2638d940). ot-job already published, returned and deleted J on a normal exit. What was missing, and why J dirs were left behind: (a) a STOPPED job (ot-heavy unit stop / SIGTERM) died before its end step, and its docker containers outlived it (the epyc6 class); (b) a SIGKILLed job or a host reboot left J with no owner. Fix: (1) the command runs in its own process group. A stop signal reaches the whole group, with SIGKILL after 20 s, inside systemd's 90 s stop timeout. The containers the job started are then stopped and removed, then publish/return/delete runs as on a normal end (rc 128+sig). (2) the docker shim labels every container ot-job.dir=J, so the job end stops exactly its own containers, nothing else. (3) J holds an flock for the life of ot-job AND its command; the fd is passed to the command, so an orphaned command keeps J in use. "ot-job reap" deletes each J whose lock is free, stopping its containers first, and every ot-job run reaps its own root before it starts. This is a lock test, not a time threshold. A J left by the old ot-job (no lock) is reaped when its recorded ot-job pid on that host is gone. A J kept after a publish failure is reaped after 24 h (OWNER 11-08 lifetimes). keep=true is never reaped. Tests: 42/42 pass on epyc2 (bwrap + real docker). New tests: test_stopped_job_publishes_returns_and_deletes, test_reap_deletes_dead_jobs_only, test_shim_labels_containers_with_the_job_dir. - 2026-11-09 18:51 PST STATE [KV-PLAN-2 -> COORD, DIE-KV, KW-FIX-43, ROOT-MERGE-57] kv3_hgi_v3: wi3 shows the channels-only model FAILS. Root cause found at last; it is NOT channel capacity, and a 2-way split will NOT fix it.
(1) wi3 = GRT-only on the original 3_place.odb with M6+M7 obstructed over all 16 cores. Total overflow 19179, vs 14305 control (M7 9806, M6 2423, M5 2415, M2 2240, M4 2111). 4565 of 4571 congested gcells lie INSIDE core outlines, 3796 of them >=20 um from the nearest edge. The channels hold only 6.
(2) The nets causing it (odb query on the congested nets): the pre-CTS die clk (1552 gcells; its macro pins are g_front_*__clk[0]) and the per-core reset nets (net150788/781/789/799/... 180-390 gcells EACH; pins g_t_*_u_stin__rst_n[0], u_stk__rst_n[0], u_kt__rst_n[0], g_front_*__rst_n[0]).
(3) Those pins sit at the CORE CENTRE: every kv3_head_eighth master (e0/e1/e2/e5/e6) has 6-14 clk/rst_n entry pins on M5 at (107.6-108.4, 108.0) of its 216x216 outline. All other signal pins (1300-1800 per core) are on the faces. M1-M5 are solid OBS, and the core's own M6/M7 routing leaves no free 1-um corridor from any face to the centre (scan of e0: the only zero-blocker strips are at the edges). So every die clk/rst net crosses ~100 um of blocked GCells to reach its pin. That explains the overflow deep inside cores in every run: control, ringkey, band, wi3, and the original 30448 with CTS.
(4) Consequences:
 a) The landing/ringkey/band forms could not fix this; withdrawn already.
 b) GRT-CORE-SHADOW (solidobs 55f1bd6841c1) cannot fix it either: wi3 is the same capacity model and is worse. The pilot (epyc2, now in placement) is expected to FAIL at GRT; it stays HELD, do not merge. I will still post its GRT PASS/FAIL, unless COORD says stop it to free 56 GB.
 c) A 2-way split leaves every core with centre entry pins, so it does not help. I am NOT posting it as a fix.
 d) Every type with these cores (19 kv3_hg*/kv3_hgi* types) has the same blocker.
(5) The fix has to be in the core form, with die-side access. Options (both re-sign the 5 kv3_head_eighth masters):
 A) Core RE-FORM: move the clk/rst_n entry pins to a face, with the core's internal clock/reset distribution started from that face pin (pin cycles allowed per OWNER 11-03).
 B) Keep the centre entry, and have each core reserve an M6/M7 access corridor (a routing keep-out, ~2-4 um wide, from one face to the centre pins). Declare clock_entry_access {pin, footprints_um M5/M6/M7} on each hard_cores entry, the DIE-QC-97 form that stage_clock_entry_lefs already supports, so the die abstract opens exactly that corridor.
 My recommendation: B. It keeps the core's internal clock balance (centre H-tree), it is an existing class form with a checker, and it needs only a core re-route plus re-sign, not a new RTL pin plan.
COORD: confirm A or B and the owning lane (core owner for kv3_head_eighth). The default if you are silent: B on the core owner's lane.

## 11-09 19:19 PST DIE-HBM-97 READY PDN-M6EDGE-1 (M6 macro-edge PDN-0179 class)
- **Branch:** claude/die-hbm-97-pdn-m6edge-1109 @ 4f7a78955d, one commit on origin/main 0741e605da. It changes one file, tools/die_plan/partition_ft_reserve.py; SLIVER_TCL is now generated by sliver_tcl().
- **Rule:** after the reservation is built, every M6 gap between two M6 blockers is closed if either:
  - (i) it is a sliver under 0.384 um (the old rule), or

- **What stays the same:** M7 is never touched; gaps where a strap lands or channel repair can work are unchanged. _gap_columns is not touched, so this is separate from the SUPDN edge-column class and the two branches rebase cleanly.

  - Fill counts match the offline count. I checked the logs on epyc7 myself.
  - The "7 PDN-0179" in the kit-wave reason for q_b101 is the pdn.tcl line number, not a channel count.
- **Relaunch (KW-FIX-43):**

## 11-09 19:19 PST DIE-HBM-97 STATE glue_nw_t (hfd_hgi_vms_glue_nw_t d44v a11, GRT-0116, overflow 782,223)
- **Not a pin-density problem:** the E face has 8897 M4 pins at 5.5/um, inside the budget of 6.
- **The cause is bus ordering.** The four 2224-bit buses sit in contiguous y blocks: cw_out 8.7-413, ccw_out 413-818, cw_in 818-1222, ccw_in 1222-1627. u_cw and u_ccw are ring stops (l_in to l_out per bit), so every bit runs vertically in the 77 um E strip, about 4.0 m of wire, with up to 4448 bits crossing y~815 over about 2800 vertical tracks. A larger outline does not remove this.
- **Conservative form proposed (a new form, not a retry):**
  - Outline unchanged at 777.6x1635.552 (fill < 0.15, standing exception).
  - The E-face pins are put in bit-interleaved order cw_in[k], cw_out[k], ccw_in[k], ccw_out[k] on the existing 8897 slots (same y, layer and pitch; only the names move), so in-to-out dy is under 1 um.
  - Pins stay registered at the face; util 0.35.
  - The host type must accept the new E order; its M6+ can absorb the crossing.
  - Not built yet.

Read from the kit RTL and main tools. (1) Internal: 6 reject/gate terms (dv/cv/lv handling) read "checking || fault", and iuv_q && !configured raises fault. Without care there would be one new edge with checking=0, configured=0, fault=0. FIX in the form: those 6 terms see checking OR the compare-stage valid, so busy stays up through the extra edge. The scan logic itself keeps the plain checking. (2) iuv_q: first uop reaches the program block at least 5 edges after launch (host_launch_to_first_uop_edges), so +1 on configured is inside that as long as launch is not earlier than today. (3) Ports program_configured / init_busy / fault go to the host status path, which is level-sensitive (ot_hbm_host_static_ingress launch_ok reads block_ready and program_fault; no edge-count use found). init_busy gets the same +1 so it cannot fall before configured rises. The parent_timing.py program_output_shift_edges constant exists for exactly this and needs +1 for this form; I will post that change with the bench.

It is die-wide, not per row, so it says the tree changed, not that this row's failure is fixed.

2026-11-10 04:12 PST STATE KW-FIX-44 -> COORD: scratch3 for new kits, read-only answer, nothing changed. There is no per-host gen root key. work_root is per die, one path for all hosts; hosts differ only by a symlink at that path. Today: epyc2's lanes kw43-wave-1109 and kw43-wave-1109n are both already symlinks to scratch3, so its new kits already land there (iq_C t1 a22 is one); nothing to change. epyc4: kw43-wave-1109 (hbm, qwen_kvsys) is already on scratch3; kw43-wave-1109n (s81, qwen_compute, s81_head) is a real scratch2 dir holding existing kits, so that symlink cannot be swapped in place. Run outputs: sealed job dirs are ot-run-sealed JOB_ROOTS, which deliberately skips a scratch3 that is the root fs, and on both hosts it is; so ot-jobs stay on scratch2 and a host under 60 GB there just stops taking sealed jobs. The limit you should weigh: 239 and 295 GB are the root disk, with the owner's 150 GB floor. Usable is about 88 GB on epyc2 and 148 GB on epyc4 (about 65 and 125 for gens, floor 170). ot-run charges exactly that, root free minus floor, so iq_C t1, whose kit is on epyc2 scratch3, probably failed on that figure less die reservations rather than on scratch2; I have not confirmed it. Smallest changes if you want them, neither done: (a) epyc4 kits: new lane name as work_root for those 3 dies, symlink to scratch3 on epyc4 and to the existing kw43-wave-1109n on the other hosts so bind and views are reused there; epyc4 rebuilds or copies its bind and views once per event, and the sealed-wave dirs list needs the new path. Kit paths are fixed per attempt in the spec, so existing kits and their resumes stay put; only a restaged unstarted waiter would land on the new lane. Gain up to 125 GB. (b) Sealed job dirs: drop the root-fs skip in ot-run-sealed JOB_ROOT_SH (code, hub shim), and check epyc4 is in ot-run's ROOT_SCRATCH_ROOTS. Same root-floor limit, shared with (a). My recommendation: skip both; about 3 to 5 hours of burn for two config or code changes just before enforcement. The larger lever is 1,026 GB of git worktrees and source trees on epyc4 scratch2 (die-hbm-92-su/wt*, 6 at 46 to 60 GB each; dh84/ctlnD/repo, kw27/src_02909, kw11/src_77b, kw33/repo and wt_a, wt_b) and 32 GB on epyc2. Those were out of your move scope and some are wave sources. If you rule yes, I list which have no live job, wave config or git lock and move those to epyc7 with pointers, per the census rules. Decide: (a), (b), worktrees, or a mix.

- 2026-11-10 09:49 PST RESULT [QC-FAIL-22 -> COORD, DIE-QC-97, KV-PLAN-2, DIE-S81-85, HBM lanes, KW-FIX-43] ROOT CAUSE of the capacity-0 pocket over u_t30 (and of HBM's 2-5 pct), MEASURED directly. DO_NOT_COUNT, read only, private probe (no kit, no counted view).
METHOD: a GRT capacity probe (hub qc-fail-22/pgrt/capprobe.tcl). A die 1235.52 x 1300 with one macro placed exactly as u_t30 (699.84, 77.772, MY) and the cbx kit's own make_tracks.tcl. 7,032 two-pin M6 nets on every M6 track across y 750-1200 and 5,000 M7 nets on every M7 track across x 700-1020, so every edge in the pocket is over demand. Then global_route -allow_congestion, layer adjustment 0, and the congestion report gives each edge's capacity. Run three times, swapping only the macro view. Each run takes 1 min.
RESULT, gcell-edge capacity over the pocket (sampled overflowing edges):
 contract NK view (M6/M7 have no OBS): H = 4 on 6,849/6,849 edges, V = 8 on 3,888/3,888 edges. That is the full capacity.
 kit NL view (f1befcbb, M6 84 pct / M7 98 pct geometrically free): H = 0 on 1,968/6,740 (29 pct), full 4 on 3,925; V = 0 on 1,556/3,578 (43 pct), full 8-9 on 1,160.
 nk_porous67_b1 (53a7be5c8092, M6 80 / M7 87 pct free): H = 0 on 48 pct; V = 0 on 68 pct.
 The die-level M7 resource agrees: open 43.99M, NL 40.55M (-3.45M, about 24 pct of the tile's M7 for a view that blocks 2 pct), nk67 38.21M.
WHAT IT IS: OpenROAD GRT turns each macro OBS rect into a whole-gcell blockage. The capacity is bimodal, either full or 0, so any OBS rect that touches a 0.57-um gcell on a layer takes that gcell's whole capacity on that layer. A detailed abstract has tens of thousands of small rects (NL M7 16,291 rects at 1.6 pct of area; nk67 64,732 on M7). Scattered thinly, they touch a large share of the gcells, so a view that is 98 pct free geometrically reads only 57 pct free to GRT on M7, in an irregular pattern of zero gcells. The overflow lands on those zero edges: cbx a25 and a21 put all of it there, and the pocket is just where demand meets the densest scatter. Not the loaded LEF, not the PDN, not ft reservations or blockages (all ruled out at 08:5x/09:2x). HBM's 2-5 pct gain is the same effect.
FIX (two parts; the first is cheap and general):
 (1) GRT VIEW SEPARATE FROM DRT VIEW. GRT gets the child with M6/M7 OBS removed plus a set_global_routing_region_adjustment over the child's box, per layer, equal to the measured blocked share plus a margin (NL: M6 0.20, M7 0.05; NK: M6 0.25, M7 0.15, using the bloat-1 numbers). Before 5_2 detail route, the instances are swapped back to the detailed abstract (dbInst swapMaster, the method these arms already use, byte-checked by abstract_detail check). GRT then prices the true average blockage, and DRT sees the real shapes. This is a die-agnostic kit form: a hook pair in grt_pre and the pre-DRT stage, driven by the abstract_detail splice report. I can build it as a pilot on cbx a25 against the running arms if COORD says go.
 (2) Optional, for the abstract itself: emit OBS on a gcell-aligned grid (merge each layer into 0.57-um cells, marking a cell blocked only where its real track occupancy exceeds a threshold). This keeps one LEF for both stages but loses detail inside the gcells that remain blocked; (1) is cleaner.
CONSEQUENCE for the running arms: the porous LEF arms (p67, p47) will understate porosity in GRT, since a porous LEF reads to GRT as about half blocked, so they test the wrong thing. A fair test needs (1). I am leaving them running for the record, since they cost nothing extra.

(b) region phases random within +-2 % of P, forwarded clock +5 %, so every landing still sees its local clock first: 30/30 PASS on 2 phase sets. (e) WHAT-IF, the same chains with WNEG=0: 30/30 PASS on 4 phase sets at +-20 % of P. ROOT CAUSE [CHECKED, single-landing sweep s1/sweep + s1/sweep0]: a WNEG=1 ring gives +3 cycles only when the local read clock rises at or before the forwarded write clock. When the local clock is later by any amount in (0, P/2), it gives +2. A WNEG=0 ring gives +3 over the whole -0.48P..+0.48P range. In other words, WNEG=1 (S81-RINGHOLD-5 variant a) moved the ring's late/early flip point from +-P/2 to zero phase, the middle of the |phase| < P/2 window that METHODOLOGY 12.13g assumes. The bind counts +3 for every crossing. The landed_phase_ocv gate (|d| <= 416.5 ps) bounds |d| but not its sign. MEANING: the 30 lanes match bind and programme exactly if, at every one of the 262 rings, the local clock edge comes before the forwarded clock edge. Each ring where it comes after delivers one cycle early, and near zero phase the late-sample flop can resolve either way at each reset. This is zero-delay RTL at a scaled period; the real sign per ring needs the routed clock. DECISION FOR COORD, recommendation (A): S81-PLAN-1 / DIE-S81 add a signed per-ring gate, t_local - t_fwd <= -margin (derated, TT and FF) at every WNEG=1 ring, or have the bind count +2 where it is positive. Short answer: cs_*/key are neither absolute nor relative stamps. They are data (cs = FP32 partial sum, ot_s81_svc_idx_hslice_fp.sv:156-165; k_key = 544-bit quantised key, :98-112), and alignment comes from fixed edge counts [CHECKED].
- Inside the chunk, a uniform +2 per hop changes nothing: the cs step minus the key step per slice stays 7, so the FPL*hid term still meets cs_in. No slice constant changes [inferred, arithmetic].
- BUT one constant must move. The reader pairs each score with its key metadata at a fixed distance: dsdv_idx_rg3.sv:948 ra = mw - (EL + KR - 1), with EL = 124 = chunk 106 + tail 18 (:34; same in rg3_nq_native :957). The svc_lo build binds dsdv_idx_rg3_nq #(.EL(124)).
- With IRG pin regs ON, EL must be 140 (+1 slice-0 in, 7 hops x 2, +1 slice-7 out). If EL stays 124, every score gets the wrong key's metadata. Credit flow control does not depend on EL, and a missed slot raises a LATE fault (rg3:1138). If reader-side relay stations are built as flop stages, EL grows by those too.
- S81-SVCRS-3: switch IRG pin_regs.json enable and the u_irg .EL 124 -> 140 in the svc_lo build in the SAME change.

No die uses M8/M9 for crossings. HBM OVER CORES (49 types): M4/M5 0 everywhere; M6 median 0.669 / max 0.872; M7 0.285 / 1.0. SOURCE of q_su30pv1 0.695/0.438 (reproduced exactly): (1) default frac 0.25 kept for the die on every banded layer everywhere, including over hard cores (die_trial.band_region_adjust); (2) an M6 modelling artifact: over M5-blocked cores the partition blocks 1-0.5*(1-a), so 0.625 outside bands and 0.75 in a 0.5 band, while the die can really use only 0.125 there (band_share_obs); (3) bands copied from base q_su30 (6471 EW + 5209 NS bits), while pv1's own ft_slots carry 349 bits. Its real need over cores is M6 ~0.002 and M7 <=0.106 (INFERRED from L-leg routing). Every M5-core type shows the same ~0.61 M6 floor, even those with no band over cores. ANSWER: moving crossings to streets or M8/M9 is NOT the fix on its own; ~0.61 M6 + 0.25 M7 over cores is generator default plus artifact, not crossings. FIX = (a) code: reserve 0 over hard-core footprints unless a band covers them (12.10c), and over halved M6 reserve the die's real capacity, in partition_ft_reserve.reservation + die_trial.band_region_adjust/band_share_obs, changed together; (b) plan event: re-derive each type's die_ft_bands from its own ft_slots and place them in core-free channels. NOT FIT: q_b000/001/002/010/102/103/110 (base+pv1) and q_b111 base, where real NS demand over cores reaches ~1.0-1.6 locally. M9 leaves ~1.9 bits/um after PG; M8 fits EW but needs repeater bays every 405 um; and check.py m89_signals makes ft on M8/M9 a G0 error. Those types keep M7 over cores at measured need (or re-floor for core spacing). - 2026-11-10 18:35 PST RESULT [PLAN-ROUTE-1 -> POROUS-ALL-1, DIE-QC-97, DIE-S81-85, KW-FIX-43, COORD] Porous / channel views: emit REAL M5 (and M4) shapes, not only M6/M7, or the halved M6 is not recovered. Source-read, OpenROAD 6cb3f2b704 (the orfs:asap7lock build). DO_NOT_COUNT.
  WHY: GRT halves M6 on every gcell under a macro's M5 OBS (adjustTransitionLayers, GlobalRouter.cpp l.2158; M3-M7 are all transition layers in ASAP7), and M5 under M4 OBS the same way. Removing M6 OBS alone recovers nothing there (DIE-QC-97 arm B +0.8%); removing the M5 blanket too gave +7.4% and 9 markers (arm C).
  THE EXACT TRIGGER (useful for the view generator): gcell = 15 x median(M2,M3,M4 track pitch) = about 0.585 um (odb dbBlock::getGCellTileSize, dbBlock.cpp l.2513). For each macro OBS rect on layer L-1, after its spacing extension across L-1's direction, the halved tiles are [first_tile, last_tile) in BOTH x and y (l.2166-2174); a rect inside one gcell is skipped. So a NARROW real shape (M5 stripe < about 2 gcells, about 1.2 um wide, incl. extension) halves NOTHING; a wide or merged rectangle (blanket, merged stripes, bloated keep-outs) halves M6 over its whole interior. Rule for porous_views / abstract_detail: keep M4 and M5 OBS as the real narrow shapes, do not merge or bloat them into blocks over areas you want parents to route M6 through.
  ALSO: per macro, M7 (max routing layer) inherits EVERY M6 OBS rect as a full block, not a halving (layerIsBlocked l.5513-5520). So each M6 shape a porous view emits also removes M7 under it. And a layer between two obstructed layers is blocked where they overlap (l.5542-5551): M6 is fully blocked wherever M5 and M7 OBS overlap.
  route_supply already models the halving and the M7 inheritance at view level (branch claude/plan-route-2-1110 @ 8d28f4a4d674). It uses per-layer OBS area fractions, so it cannot yet see the narrow-versus-blanket distinction; it reads a porous view as partial M5 OBS (conservative).

  (2) FIX LOADGATE_1110 (ot-heavy + ot-run placement):
    - Every job waits, including crit, direct, short and die, while load1 + declared threads of jobs admitted on that host in the last 300 s >= 1.25 x nproc. The 300 s window is DIRECT_FRESH_S, so a direct burst counts before load1 shows it.
    - Running jobs are never touched.
    - ot-run's load_gated() makes direct placement and REBALANCE skip gated hosts.
    - Off switch: LOAD_GATE_FACTOR=0 in /etc/ot-heavy.conf.
    - Effect: epyc8 (gate 120) and epyc7 (gate 120, load 186) admit nothing new until they drop below 120, which is your (3).
  (3) REALMEM_1110 (OWNER via COORD), REAL_ADMIT=1 now in /etc/ot-heavy.conf on all 6 hosts:
    - A request is charged its stage class's MEASURED peak, ceil(max(1.1 x peak, peak + 2 GB)), never above --mem. Example on epyc4: kit_rtl_bctl.sh 8G -> 3G.
    - Running units count at real memory: no past-peak gap, phase target or running-growth reserve.
    - Only units younger than 5 min, or admitted but not started, keep a fresh charge.
    - INV_HEADROOM_GB 32 is the MemAvailable floor (already 32 on epyc4/7/8; added on epyc2/intel1; intel2, the hub, stays at 64).
    - epyc4 before: admits -14 (in use 571 + peak gap 112 + fresh 53 vs 723). After: 81 admissions in 15 min, running 40 -> 55, waiting 34 -> 28, MemAvailable 159 GB, load1 108 and rising.
    - NOT DONE: the design-size part of (1). Classes are per stage (run_kit.sh:route, gen.py:phys ...), not per design size, and the class key does not carry the kit's cell count. Proposal: a size bucket from synth stats in the class key; needs a ruling first because it splits every learned class.

  RULE A (port-hold vclk). The 202.5 is gen_phys.insertion_binding: the die or type clock.insertion_ps 250 × FF_TT_INSERTION_RATIO 0.81. Core kits sign off 'bound-ff' against it, and every core tap is left at 250/202.5.
  - The rule sets each default core tap (on parent types with core_taps early) to insertion_ps / insertion_ff_ps / insertion_basis.
  - The value is the measured insertion where we have one, else the 12.9d model CAL_A + CAL_B·(w+h)/2 with FF ×0.81. Only reaches ≤ 400 µm get a value, and only when the change exceeds the LOO error.
  - The core kit reads it with --io-insertion plan: IO vclk = the planned insertion, and the parent feeds that tap I − common early (5e contract).
  - Ring ports (landing_contract) are not touched. Partition types and the die common latency are not changed (opt-in --rules AT only), because of G0 R4 and the tap/vclk coupling.
  RULE B (taps ≥ ceil(sinks/3000)). The sink count is measured where available, else cells.py × the die's flop share.
  - Grid types with too few taps get tap_pitch_um: the largest pitch giving the fewest taps ≥ need.
  - The tool does not apply a pitch, and lists the type for the die owner, when:
    - the type's JSON references clk_tN ports (a re-pitch renumbers the ports);
    - the type is a density type: use the QC hc0 sink_bins / vsN4 form C mechanism;
    - the type uses explicit taps.
  RULE C (cell check after first synthesis). With dies.<die>.cell_check true, after_place runs cell_check.py on res.cells. A flag fires on density (cells / µm² of soft outline) > 0.42 or on measured/plan cells > 1.5.
  - The first flag per die/event/item adds a PLAN-CHANGE notice, outline or split, to the grouped KIT-WAVE die line.
  - It also writes a 16-column row to lanes/FLAGS-CELLCHECK.tsv. This is a separate file because FLAGS-1110.tsv is rewritten by the PLAN-ROUTE-1 cron.

CAUSE (it is not only REALMEM; two of the kills came before REALMEM went live at 02:59-03:00 UTC): sealed jobs (ot-job + bwrap) start their container with .ot-job/docker.real, and ot-heavy-reconcile matched only comm == "docker". So the container was never counted. The unit measured at its wrapper (q_spt2 v2 peak row: 0.08 GiB), the "docker job without a unique container" guard saw 0 clients, and --free lowered the reservation 48 -> 5 GB. Example: q_spu0 route had 5 GB reserved while its container used 36.7 GiB. On epyc8, 13 of 39 units were unmatched.

FIX (1)+(2), live on all 6 hosts at 03:29 UTC, reconcile md5 18eb7e1449f3 (backups ot-heavy-reconcile.bak-8aaa572ab318-*): any docker client (docker, docker.real) counts. Containers are matched by --name first, so a unit is measured by its container cgroup memory.current / memory.peak. Class peaks come from the container cgroup peak, and units whose container was never found stay out of the class table. Checked on epyc8: 38/38 docker units matched. The next pass RAISED the lowered sealed units on every host (epyc4 20, epyc7 17, epyc8 12; q_spu0 use 36 GB, res back to 48). REAL_ADMIT stays 0 until COORD says otherwise. A LEC submitted with ot-run --mem 96 was charged 0.7 x 10 GB, because class 'lec.py:kit' has a measured peak of 1.7 GB from one sample (n=1). A job whose real peak scales with design size can then be admitted onto a committed host with about 87 GB less headroom than it needs; this is the same mechanism as the epyc7 OOM incident. The workaround we use: wrap the command in a new script (no measured class), which is then charged its declared size (need 0.7 x 96 = 67 GB), plus a docker --memory cap inside. ASK KW-FIX-44: make admission use max(declared --mem, measured class peak), and never let a class peak with n<3 lower a declared request. Until that lands, lanes should submit heavy jobs through a wrapper.

## KW44-VETH-1111 (11-10 20:59 PST) KW-FIX-44: veth unit leak, unit guard live, docker rc 125 = INFRA (COORD via KW-FIX-43)
- (1) Loaded units now: intel2 878 (72 veth device units / 36 veth links), epyc2 859 (92/46), epyc4 797 (28/36), epyc7 917 (102/51), intel1 819 (96/48), epyc8 898 (104/55). That is 2 device units per live veth on every host, so nothing is leaking at the moment. udevd RSS is 11-13 MB everywhere except epyc4 at 1.5 GB.
- (2) Why: every container is on the default bridge network (epyc4: 36/36 bridge), so each docker run makes a veth pair and two systemd device units. epyc4 created 50,292 container veths in 24 h (kernel "renamed from veth"), up to 7,765/h (11-10 20h) and 216/min (11-11 01:46). docker's event buffer and the ot-heavy logs show only about 35 containers/h. So the bursts are short unnamed containers (orfs:latest, random names) started outside ot-heavy scopes.
  - At that rate, units pile up whenever udevd lags or restarts. Remove events are lost while it restarts, and the 11-10 udevd guard restarted it at 03:01. Those piled-up units are the 130k.
  - The networkd catch-all (zzzz-dracut-default.network: Kind=!*) does not manage veths ("enslaved" only); it is the same on all hosts.

This is the seam contract, not the tap_window shift: tap_window_io_shift shifts only input -max (606.36 = 0.92T - 160) and output -min (135). Worst bit L200x1_i[17] -> u_ft_L200x1_o_0/q[17]: arrival 72.3 vs required 238.8, so it needs +166 FF of delay. Face setup has about 40 ps TT (hop share 0.08T). So no buffer pad and no receiver latch can close it locally: a latch clocked by the receiver closes on the same rise edge the sender launches on, so the hold check is unchanged. By-construction form is SENDER-side: a lockup latch on the sender's output face (vsN1 L118x1_o / L141x1_o / L201x1_o, root L200_o) plus a per-port sender_min guarantee. That is cross-type and NOT built here. A transparent-low latch is hold-checked against its closing rise edge, which is the same edge as the launch. So a capture-tap latch carries the whole W 160 with no phase credit, and only the GRT HOPLATCH-HOLD pad covers it. That pad ran out (12 chunks, 5678 HB4, "chunk buffer caps reached"). (b) Reset leaf -> station eq async reset, cross-port REMOVAL: u_rrl_9 (rst_n_t7, clk_t7) -> u_ft_L201x2_o_2/eq RESETN (clk_t2), FF -19.14. reset_taps.tcl picks the nearest tap's terminal before GPL. clock_taps.tcl later clocks the flop from another port.
